description:
FOUND s492b while measuring what an IMPLICIT close does to $? (#2006 (a)).  PRE-EXISTING on 5ce155cb.

PROBE (scratch/s492b/qmark.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs base vs tree -- base and tree identical):
  $? = 1792; print "a $?";                         perl 1792   PCL 0
  system("sh","-c","exit 2"); print $? >> 8;        perl 2      PCL 2     (control, right)
  $? = 0; print "c $?";                            perl 0      PCL 512

So the WRITE is lost and every READ answers the last child's wait status.  perl's $? is an ordinary writable magic scalar; programs zero it before a check (`$? = 0; ...; die if $?`), and Test::Harness-style code sets it deliberately.

WHERE: `$?` is a runtime place the generated code assigns through the ordinary scalar path, but the READ side resolves to the child-status register rather than to the assigned cell -- grep `$?` in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp (it is `setf $?` in the waitpid/close paths) and find what the emission of `$? = N` produces.

NOT A BLOCKER for #2006 (a): that fix SAVES AND RESTORES $? around the implicit close, which is perl's behaviour, and the save/restore works (it uses the same register).  What is missing is the user-visible assignment.
BAR: cl/ change => full sweep + the companion io/ and op/ legs; guard rows beside fileio-02.t's $? row (test 13).


=== DONE (s495f, 2026-09-25) ===
Fixed with #2009 (one seam): $? is a magic integer box; see #2009 DONE for the design, probes and guards (Pl/t/die-exit-status-01.t rows 13 and 14-23).
subject: BUG (pre-existing, found by the #2006(a) probes): `$? = N` does not stick -- PCL always reports the LAST CHILD'S status, so `$? = 0` before a check reads the old value and perl-shaped `$?` bookkeeping is impossible
